rows.description: A rumour about me holds a grain of truth and I feel shame. I can say yes, that happened, it is private, and stop the talk. Owning it calmly takes away much of its power.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, curiosity, fear, guilt, humiliation, loyalty
related mind states: shame, calm

rows.description: We lost the final and I am crushed. Disappointment shows I cared. Wise: cry if I need to, then congratulate the winners and think about what to practise. Throwing the bat or blaming the umpire only shows hurt pride.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, fear, resentment
related mind states: sadness, disappointment, pride, hurt

rows.description: The other team won unfairly, I think, and I cannot let go. Sometimes decisions are unfair. Wise: speak to the coach politely, then move on. Refusing to shake hands leaves me bitter and them unchanged.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, disillusionment, fear
related mind states: resentment

rows.description: I lose and still shake hands and say well played. It feels hard, but it earns respect from everyone. Wins and losses pass, and character remains.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, disillusionment, fear, resentment
related mind states: admiration

rows.description: My coach is angry after the loss and I feel scared and small. A good coach corrects the game, not the child. I listen for useful points and let go of the harsh tone. If it feels abusive, I tell a parent.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, disillusionment, resentment
related mind states: anger, fear

rows.description: My father says you should have won, and I feel I disappointed him. Some parents transfer their dreams to a child. I can tell him I did my best and need his support, not more pressure.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: compassion, disillusionment, fear, resentment
related mind states: disappointment

rows.description: I blame the slower teammate for our loss. Blame gives quick relief but breaks the team. Wise: look at what everyone, including me, could improve, and encourage her rather than shame her.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, compassion, disillusionment, fear, resentment
related mind states: shame, relief

rows.description: I dropped the catch and the team lost. I feel terrible, and a friend says everyone drops one. Her kindness lets me try again. Being harshly blamed would make me fear playing.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: coercion, disillusionment, fear, resentment
related mind states: fear, empathy

rows.description: I won and feel wonderful. Pride in effort is healthy. Wise: thank the team, be kind to the losers, and remember they feel bad. Gloating and mocking makes winning small.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: contempt, envy
related mind states: gratitude, curiosity, pride, awe

rows.description: After beating my rival, I show off and rub it in. It feels sweet for a moment but costs respect. The mature response is to be gracious, because next time I may lose.
graph_context: same situation, other stances at this age: envy, pride
related mind states: admiration, contempt
